contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #240: Shelah's eventual categoricity and the prescribed-threshold obstruction.

Audit the September 24, 2026 OpenAI AEC manuscripts. Selected target: eventual reversal of strong self-maps on every fixed infinite tuple bound at all sufficiently large categoricity cardinals, including singular ones, for an AEC categorical unboundedly often.

definitions.H(delta): the rational finite-support lexicographic sum over the integer finite-support lexicographic group on the ordinal delta; greatest differing coordinates decide order
definitions.orbit_arrow: p -> r iff a strong self-map sends a tuple from automorphism orbit p to one from orbit r
definitions.strict_slot: points outside a parameter set lying strictly between the two sides of a cut of that set

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 240 (Shelah's eventual categoricity and the prescribed-threshold obstruction.; papers: A CH obstruction to a prescribed categoricity threshold; Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/240.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

Boney-Vasey arXiv:1508.03316v2 provides restricted syntactic-characterization variants and documents a gap and withdrawn attempted repair for the unrestricted variant; it does not supply an unrestricted proof for this audit.
The existential uniform-threshold statement in main:uniform and the CH prescribed-threshold obstruction in thm:main are logically compatible at statement level; this does not verify either assertion.
For each infinite lambda there is mu(lambda)>=lambda such that every AEC with LS(K)<=lambda categorical in some kappa>=mu(lambda) is categorical in all kappa_prime>=mu(lambda).
Every AEC categorical in unboundedly many cardinals is categorical on a tail.
Under CH there exists a countable relational AEC K with LS(K)=aleph_0, at least two models at beth_(omega_2), and categoricity at every mu>=beth_((2^(aleph_1))^+).

For every infinite theta, an AEC K categorical unboundedly often admits b_K(theta) such that at every categoricity kappa>=b_K(theta), for every strong f:M->M with |M|=kappa and every tuple a of length at most theta, there is a strong g:M->M satisfying g(f(a_i))=a_i for all i; no amalgamation, cofinality restriction on kappa, or kappa^theta=kappa is assumed.
The classical L_(infinity,theta) downward LS theorem applies to the model-theoretic forcing relation used in the historical unrestricted syntactic-characterization argument.

Boney-Vasey arXiv:1508.03316v2 provides restricted syntactic-characterization variants and documents a gap and withdrawn attempted repair for the unrestricted variant; it does not supply an unrestricted proof for this audit.

claims.natural_statement: Sections 4-14: stabilized diagrams, bounded placement, working-scheme calculus, isolation, marked/geometric boundary lifting, common levels, and cardinal induction supply pointed uniqueness on a tail. These are separate, unaudited obligations.
found:small-code: an AEC with LS at most lambda is recoverable, uniformly in set theory, from a set code of its models and strong pairs of size at most lambda.
found:uniform-reduction: the qualitative and existential uniform-threshold forms of eventual categoricity are equivalent by Replacement over small codes.
found:directed-colimits: the AEC chain and coherence axioms give set-indexed directed unions, their common-upper-bound clause, and coherent strong direct limits.
found:partition: each fixed finite-arity coloring has homogeneous subsets of a prescribed cardinality above a sufficiently large cardinal; finitely many arities can be handled together.
found:order-template: arbitrarily large models yield one functorial finite-support order presentation with at most LS(K) labels and strong subpresentations, of size |I|+LS(K) on infinite orders.
found:order-basic: H(delta) has size |delta|, point character cf(delta), homogeneous bounded intervals and rays, and finite ordinal-support comparison codes.
found:balanced-cuts: every interior nonprincipal cut of Gamma_delta and H(delta) has equal left and right characters.

found:cut-segments: in the specified homogeneous dense order, a segment approaching a balanced cut of regular character epsilon below the point character has type determined by epsilon, direction, and endpoint.
found:order-orbits: for theta<cf(delta), short sequences in H(delta) have the same order-automorphism orbit exactly when their diagrams and all strict-slot occupancies agree.
found:orbit-bound: at every categoricity kappa>=max(LS(K),theta^+), including singular kappa, theta-tuple automorphism orbits number at most B=2^(2^(LS(K)+theta)).
The named orbit-arrow relation and partial record-to-name map have a set-sized palette of at most 2^B profiles, uniform in size and presentation ordinal.

found:ordinal-support-closure: for theta^+<=a<cf(beta), every at-most-a support set extends to a bounded T0 of size at most a and cofinality above theta, matching every finite ordinal pattern over every at-most-theta subset.

found:append-segment: appending a consecutive indecomposable delta after T0 preserves finite-pattern matching over at-most-theta parameters, yields order type delta, and reflects every short H-slot occupancy.
found:alignment: common-profile presentations at a<mu yield a strong a-sized submodel containing any prescribed at-most-a set, with every theta-tuple's small and large orbit names equal.
found:indecomposable-occurrences: indecomposable ordinals of size kappa and any prescribed infinite regular cofinality tau<=kappa occur cofinally below kappa^+.
Unboundedly many failing categoricity sizes yield a<mu with a^theta<=mu, a common cofinally recurring profile, and a mu-presentation ordinal of cofinality greater than a.
An orbit unable to reach p cannot regain reachability under any strong map between mu-sized copies, including the canonical inclusion into every mu-sized limit union.
With the common profile and alignment, theta^+ rounds processing all a^theta small tuples force a final a-sized model with no tuple able to reach an orbit p that occurs there, a contradiction.
aec:class: the companion construction satisfies all AEC axioms with LS(K)=aleph_0, including directed unions and smoothness.
Section 4: rank functions modulo countable sets and coherent countable extensional diagrams produce an uncountable-base object of size beth_(omega_2), distinct from a countable-base object.
end:diagrams: the tuplewise countable membership diagrams have exact subsequence restrictions and pass all validity tests outside their countable exceptional sets.
col:no-pattern: no sequence of one color per finite arity passes every full-subsequence test; its coherent tagged extensional limit would inject too large a set into V_(omega_1).
cat:bounded: an object with uncountable base has fewer than Lambda=beth_((2^(aleph_1))^+) index points, by finite-arity partition and exception-set selection.
cat:countable-base: two countable-base objects with equally sized index sorts are isomorphic by finite row/column translator allocation.
cat:tail: models exist at every mu>=Lambda and must have countable base, yielding categoricity via the countable-base classification.

For arbitrary ordinal-position families with the same strict order pattern, transporting unchanged integer and rational coefficient codes preserves both levels of greatest-differing-coordinate comparison and every strict-slot witness inequality. This is a technical core, not the full reversal theorem.

For every reflexive transitive orbit-arrow relation, an irreversible arrow permits elimination of reachability to its source; exclusion persists under every direct transition, including to a limit. A covered union whose tuple names receive arrows from processed excluded names cannot realize the source orbit. This is a technical core, not the full reversal theorem.

For arbitrary same-pattern ordinal-position codes, nested integer/rational leading-coordinate comparisons and strict slots are preserved. For arbitrary ordinal delta and coordinate type C with mk(C)<cf(delta), increasing-stage coverage captures every tuple in one stage. In every reflexive transitive orbit-arrow relation, an irreversible arrow permits reachability elimination, exclusion persists under direct arrows to all later stages including limits, and the explicit cleared/aligned ordinal-round criterion contradicts final realization of the eliminated orbit. This is a technical-core theorem, not a formalization of the full AEC reversal theorem.
claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib

universe u

namespace ReversalAudit

def SamePattern {I A B : Type*} [LT A] [LT B]
    (x : I → A) (y : I → B) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j, x i < x j ↔ y i < y j

theorem equality_transport {I A B : Type*} [LinearOrder A] [LinearOrder B]
    {x : I → A} {y : I → B} (h : SamePattern x y) (i j : I) :
    x i = x j ↔ y i = y j := by
  constructor
  · intro hx
    apply le_antisymm
    · apply le_of_not_gt
      intro hj
      have hh := (h j i).mpr hj
      simpa [hx] using hh
    · apply le_of_not_gt
      intro hi
      have hh := (h i j).mpr hi
      simpa [hx] using hh
  · intro hy
    apply le_antisymm
    · apply le_of_not_gt
      intro hj
      have hh := (h j i).mp hj
      simpa [hy] using hh
    · apply le_of_not_gt
      intro hi
      have hh := (h i j).mp hi
      simpa [hy] using hh

def LeadingLT {I A C : Type*} [LT A] [LT C]
    (positions : I → A) (c d : I → C) : Prop :=
  ∃ i, c i < d i ∧ ∀ j, positions i < positions j → c j = d j

theorem leadingLT_transport {I A B C : Type*} [LT A] [LT B] [LT C]
    {x : I → A} {y : I → B} (h : SamePattern x y) (c d : I → C) :
    LeadingLT x c d ↔ LeadingLT y c d := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨i, hi, htail⟩
    exact ⟨i, hi, fun j hj => htail j ((h i j).mpr hj)⟩
  · rintro ⟨i, hi, htail⟩
    exact ⟨i, hi, fun j hj => htail j ((h i j).mp hj)⟩

def NestedLT {I A J : Type*} [LT A]
    (positions : I → A) (ranks : J → I → ℤ) (c d : J → ℚ) : Prop :=
  ∃ i, c i < d i ∧ ∀ j, LeadingLT positions (ranks i) (ranks j) → c j = d j

theorem nestedLT_transport {I A B J : Type*} [LT A] [LT B]
    {x : I → A} {y : I → B} (h : SamePattern x y)
    (ranks : J → I → ℤ) (c d : J → ℚ) :
    NestedLT x ranks c d ↔ NestedLT y ranks c d := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨i, hi, htail⟩
    exact ⟨i, hi, fun j hj => htail j ((leadingLT_transport h _ _).mpr hj)⟩
  · rintro ⟨i, hi, htail⟩
    exact ⟨i, hi, fun j hj => htail j ((leadingLT_transport h _ _).mp hj)⟩

def InSlot {I A J P : Type*} [LT A]
    (positions : I → A) (ranks : J → I → ℤ)
    (parameters : P → J → ℚ) (lower : P → Prop) (w : J → ℚ) : Prop :=
  (∀ p, lower p → NestedLT positions ranks (parameters p) w) ∧
    (∀ p, ¬ lower p → NestedLT positions ranks w (parameters p))

theorem slot_transport {I A B J P : Type*} [LT A] [LT B]
    {x : I → A} {y : I → B} (h : SamePattern x y)
    (ranks : J → I → ℤ) (parameters : P → J → ℚ)
    (lower : P → Prop) (w : J → ℚ) :
    InSlot x ranks parameters lower w ↔ InSlot y ranks parameters lower w := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hl, hu⟩
    exact ⟨fun p hp => (nestedLT_transport h _ _ _).mp (hl p hp),
      fun p hp => (nestedLT_transport h _ _ _).mp (hu p hp)⟩
  · rintro ⟨hl, hu⟩
    exact ⟨fun p hp => (nestedLT_transport h _ _ _).mpr (hl p hp),
      fun p hp => (nestedLT_transport h _ _ _).mpr (hu p hp)⟩

theorem bounded_stages {T : Type u} {δ : Ordinal.{u}}
    (hcard : Cardinal.mk T < δ.cof) (stage : T → Ordinal.{u})
    (hstage : ∀ t, stage t < δ) :
    ∃ i, i < δ ∧ ∀ t, stage t ≤ i :=
  ⟨⨆ t, stage t, Ordinal.iSup_lt_of_lt_cof hcard hstage,
    Ordinal.le_iSup stage⟩

theorem tuple_capture {T : Type u} {X : Type*} {δ : Ordinal.{u}}
    (hcard : Cardinal.mk T < δ.cof) (A : Ordinal.{u} → Set X)
    (hmono : Monotone A) (tuple : T → X)
    (hcover : ∀ t, ∃ i, i < δ ∧ tuple t ∈ A i) :
    ∃ i, i < δ ∧ ∀ t, tuple t ∈ A i := by
  classical
  choose stage hstage hmem using hcover
  obtain ⟨i, hi, hbound⟩ := bounded_stages hcard stage hstage
  exact ⟨i, hi, fun t => hmono (hbound t) (hmem t)⟩

def Excluded {Q : Type*} (R : Q → Q → Prop) (p q : Q) : Prop :=
  ¬ R q p

theorem excluded_forward {Q : Type*} {R : Q → Q → Prop}
    (htrans : Transitive R) {p q q' : Q} (h : Excluded R p q)
    (hstep : R q q') : Excluded R p q' :=
  fun hback => h (htrans hstep hback)

theorem eliminate_orbit {Q : Type*} {R : Q → Q → Prop}
    (hrefl : Reflexive R) (htrans : Transitive R)
    {p r : Q} (hpr : R p r) (hrp : ¬ R r p) (q : Q) :
    ∃ q', R q q' ∧ Excluded R p q' := by
  classical
  by_cases hqp : R q p
  · exact ⟨r, htrans hqp hpr, hrp⟩
  · exact ⟨q, hrefl q, hqp⟩

theorem limit_persistence {I Q : Type*} [Preorder I]
    {R : Q → Q → Prop} (htrans : Transitive R)
    (name : I → Q)
    (transition : ∀ i j, i ≤ j → R (name i) (name j))
    {i : I} {p : Q} (h : Excluded R p (name i)) :
    ∀ j, i ≤ j → Excluded R p (name j) :=
  fun j hij => excluded_forward htrans h (transition i j hij)

theorem covered_union_exclusion {I T Q : Type*}
    {R : Q → Q → Prop} (htrans : Transitive R)
    (p : Q) (contains : I → T → Prop)
    (processed aligned : I → T → Q) (finalName : T → Q)
    (capture : ∀ t, ∃ i, contains i t)
    (cleared : ∀ i t, contains i t → Excluded R p (processed i t))
    (handoff : ∀ i t, contains i t →
      ∃ j, R (processed i t) (aligned j t) ∧ R (aligned j t) (finalName t)) :
    ∀ t, Excluded R p (finalName t) := by
  intro t
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := capture t
  obtain ⟨j, hlarge, hsmall⟩ := handoff i t hi
  exact excluded_forward htrans (cleared i t hi) (htrans hlarge hsmall)

theorem elimination_contradiction {I T Q : Type*}
    {R : Q → Q → Prop} (hrefl : Reflexive R) (htrans : Transitive R)
    (p : Q) (contains : I → T → Prop)
    (processed aligned : I → T → Q) (finalName : T → Q)
    (capture : ∀ t, ∃ i, contains i t)
    (cleared : ∀ i t, contains i t → Excluded R p (processed i t))
    (handoff : ∀ i t, contains i t →
      ∃ j, R (processed i t) (aligned j t) ∧ R (aligned j t) (finalName t))
    (realized : ∃ t, finalName t = p) : False := by
  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := realized
  have h := covered_union_exclusion htrans p contains processed aligned finalName
    capture cleared handoff t
  rw [ht] at h
  exact h (hrefl p)

theorem ordinal_elimination_contradiction
    {C : Type u} {X T Q : Type*} {δ : Ordinal.{u}}
    {R : Q → Q → Prop} (hrefl : Reflexive R) (htrans : Transitive R)
    (hcard : Cardinal.mk C < δ.cof)
    (A : Ordinal.{u} → Set X) (hmono : Monotone A)
    (coordinates : T → C → X)
    (hcover : ∀ t c, ∃ i, i < δ ∧ coordinates t c ∈ A i)
    (p : Q)
    (processed aligned : {i : Ordinal.{u} // i < δ} → T → Q)
    (finalName : T → Q)
    (cleared : ∀ i t, (∀ c, coordinates t c ∈ A i.val) →
      Excluded R p (processed i t))
    (handoff : ∀ i t, (∀ c, coordinates t c ∈ A i.val) →
      ∃ j, R (processed i t) (aligned j t) ∧ R (aligned j t) (finalName t))
    (realized : ∃ t, finalName t = p) : False := by
  have capture : ∀ t, ∃ i : {i : Ordinal.{u} // i < δ},
      ∀ c, coordinates t c ∈ A i.val := by
    intro t
    obtain ⟨i, hi, hmem⟩ := tuple_capture hcard A hmono (coordinates t) (hcover t)
    exact ⟨⟨i, hi⟩, hmem⟩
  exact elimination_contradiction hrefl htrans p
    (fun i t => ∀ c, coordinates t c ∈ A i.val)
    processed aligned finalName capture cleared handoff realized

end ReversalAudit

claims.natural_statement: Section 4: short strong-map classes stabilize across categoricity sizes; finite supports supply bounded comparison tests, compatible placement, and amalgamation at adequate closed levels.
Sections 5-7: finite working schemes have the required tuple calculus, free extensions, relative isolation, and all-domination with primeness and uniqueness.
Sections 8-9: adjoining finite marks preserves the working package, and every finite marked depth admits amalgamated completion and exact boundary isomorphism lifting at adequate levels.

close:uniform-definitions: fixed first-order set formulas and a fixed set of descriptors define all finite-depth construction and adequacy requests without invoking a previously selected closure function.
Section 13, marked application: one sufficiently large eligible level supports every finite marked depth and its exact lifting assertions.

Section 10: a minimal singleton type gives a pregeometry; common marked lifting rules out proper no-point-growth extensions, and a downward argument extends this to all sufficiently large pointed models, where basis size equals model size.
Sections 11-12: every finite geometric shape has the working package, classification by prescribed basis maps, and exact boundary lifting at adequate levels.
close:common-levels, geometric application: after fixing the no-growth threshold, one level supports all finite geometric shapes and their exact boundary assertions.
Section 14: a simultaneous induction on the maximum prescribed basis-piece cardinality for all finite shapes yields pointed categoricity at every sufficiently large cardinal, including limits.
end:domination: there are functions f_alpha:omega_1->omega_1 for alpha<omega_2 such that gamma<alpha implies f_gamma(beta)<f_alpha(beta) outside a countable set of beta.
end:countable-closures: each nonempty finite subset X of V_(omega_2) lies in a countable extensional membership subdiagram D_X, coherently under nonempty subset inclusions.
cat:cardinals: for xi=2^(aleph_1), Lambda=beth_(xi^+) is a strong limit of cofinality xi^+; the finite-arity partition source bounds remain below Lambda.

cat:finite-patterns: colorings of every finite arity on a set of size at least Lambda with palettes of size at most xi admit fixed arity colors realized simultaneously on a separate finite witness at every depth.
Sections 4-14 supply pointed uniqueness on a tail and placement of the fixed point pattern in every sufficiently large model. These downstream assertions remain unaudited.
Under CH, aec:class: the companion construction satisfies all AEC axioms with LS(K)=aleph_0, including directed unions and smoothness.
Under CH, Section 4: rank functions modulo countable sets and coherent countable extensional diagrams produce an uncountable-base object of size beth_(omega_2), distinct from a countable-base object.
Under CH, end:diagrams: the tuplewise countable membership diagrams have exact subsequence restrictions and pass all validity tests outside their countable exceptional sets.
Under CH, col:no-pattern: no sequence of one color per finite arity passes every full-subsequence test; its coherent tagged extensional limit would inject too large a set into V_(omega_1).
Under CH, cat:bounded: an object with uncountable base has fewer than Lambda=beth_((2^(aleph_1))^+) index points, by the whole-profile palette bound and countably many full-tuple exception sets.
For the companion construction under CH, cat:countable-base: two countable-base objects with equally sized index sorts are isomorphic by finite row/column translator allocation.
Under CH, cat:tail: models exist at every mu>=Lambda and must have countable base, yielding categoricity via the countable-base classification.
